# Rewrite a Confusing Workplace Email with Cohere

> **In short:** You can paste a long, tangled work email into Cohere and ask it to draft a short, friendly reply in plain English — for free. Always read the draft before sending, because the AI can miss a request or invent a detail.

You've opened a message from a coworker and it's a wall of words — three questions, two side requests, and a half-thought about Friday's meeting. This guide walks you through using Cohere to untangle that message and send a reply that's clear, polite, and still yours.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account — sign up at cohere.com using your email address
- The confusing email open somewhere you can copy from (your inbox, Slack, or a notes app)
- A rough idea of how you want to reply: agree, ask for more time, push back, or just acknowledge
- About 10 minutes total

## Step 1 — Copy the email you want to rewrite

Open the message that's giving you trouble. Click at the very top of the message, hold Shift, and click at the bottom so the whole thing — greeting to sign-off — is highlighted. Press **Ctrl + C** on Windows or **Cmd + C** on Mac. If the keyboard shortcut doesn't work, right-click the highlighted text and choose **Copy**. Don't copy only part of it; the AI needs the full context to make sense of the questions buried inside.

💬 Example: a tangled email to copy — "Hi, so I was thinking about the Q3 thing and wanted to circle back on what we discussed, but also there's a new issue with the Henderson account that maybe we should loop in Sarah on, and by the way did anyone book the meeting room for Friday? Let me know your thoughts. Thanks, Mark."

You'll know it worked when the message text looks dimmed or highlighted and you see a brief "Copied" pop-up on your screen.

## Step 2 — Open Cohere's chat and start fresh

In your browser, go to **cohere.com** and look for the chat area — usually a text box near the bottom with placeholder text like *"Send a message"* or *"Ask anything."* Click inside it; a blinking cursor means you're ready to type. If you've chatted with Cohere before, look for a **New chat** button (often a plus icon at the top of the sidebar) so old messages don't confuse the AI. If you don't see a sidebar, your screen is already a blank chat — that's fine, just start typing.

💬 Example: just open the page and look at the empty box. You don't need to type anything yet.

You'll know it worked when the cursor is blinking in an empty box and the page says something like *"Start a new conversation."*

## Step 3 — Tell Cohere what role to play, then paste the email

Type a short instruction that names three things: your role (a coworker replying), what you want (a polite, clear reply), and the tone (friendly, professional, brief). Then paste the original email right after. Keep your instruction to two or three sentences so the AI focuses on the right job. If pressing **Enter** doesn't send the message, look for a small **arrow button** or **paper plane icon** next to the text box and click that instead.

💬 Example: "I'm replying to this email from a coworker. Please rewrite it as a short, friendly reply that answers the questions, confirms what I can do, and asks about anything I'm unsure about. Here's the original email:" — then paste the email text on a new line.

You'll know it worked when Cohere starts typing a response (you'll see words appearing one at a time) and stops with a finished draft below.

## Step 4 — Read the draft and check it covers everything

Read Cohere's reply slowly. Put a finger on each part of the original email and confirm the draft addresses it: Did it answer the questions? Does it confirm the meeting room? Does it mention the Henderson account? If something is missing, jot a quick note — Step 5 covers fixing it. If a detail looks wrong or made-up, mark it too; AI sometimes adds facts that aren't there.

💬 Example: check the three points in Mark's email — the Q3 follow-up, the Henderson account, and the Friday meeting room — and confirm the draft mentions each one.

You'll know it worked when you can point to each part of the original email and find a matching answer, follow-up, or question in the draft.

## Step 5 — Ask Cohere to fix anything that's off

If the draft is missing something, has the wrong tone, or is just too long, tell Cohere what to change. Type a short follow-up in the same chat — like *"make it shorter"*, *"add a line asking about the Henderson account"*, or *"make the tone warmer."* Cohere will rewrite the same draft, not start over, so your edits stack. You can do this two or three times until it feels right.

💬 Example: "Good start. Can you make it half as long and add a sentence asking who's joining the Friday meeting?"

You'll know it worked when a new, shorter version appears below that includes your edits and still answers the original questions.

## Step 6 — Add your voice and send the reply

Copy Cohere's final draft and paste it into your email client. Now make it sound like you — swap any words that feel stiff, add a small personal touch ("Hope your week's going well!" or "Thanks again"), and double-check names, dates, and attachments before hitting send. The AI did the heavy lifting; you brought the human voice. Whatever you do, don't send the raw AI output — your reader will feel the difference.

💬 Example: change *"I acknowledge your update"* to *"Got it, thanks for the heads-up!"* before sending.

You'll know it worked when you can read your own email out loud and it sounds like something you'd actually say to a coworker.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting only part of the email.** The AI can't guess what's missing. Always paste the full message, including the greeting and sign-off, so it has the whole picture.
- **Asking for too many changes at once.** "Make it shorter, friendlier, more confident, and add a joke" — pick the change that matters most, then ask one thing per follow-up so the AI can actually focus.
- **Sending the AI's draft without reading it.** AI can invent facts or miss a key request. Always read the reply once out loud before you send — your name is on the message, not the AI's.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** The same trick works on a wall-of-text message from family, a neighbor, or a group chat — paste, ask for a short reply, edit to sound like you.
- **For your business or work:** You'll save real time on the back-and-forth that eats most of a workday. The first reply is the slowest; everything after gets faster because you've set the tone.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't try to use AI for every email. Start with the ones that confuse you — that's where it earns its keep fastest.

## Try it now
Open Cohere's chat, paste one email that's been sitting in your inbox for too long, and ask it to write a short reply. Don't send it yet — just see what it comes up with. You'll learn how it sounds in about two minutes.
